Fun, Fast and Fierce! I'm enjoying every minute of this game! I'm a big fan of bullet heavens and hack n' slash games and Craft Survivors is ticking all the boxes up until now. It's the first bullet heaven that I feel that there is a huge difference between each character game play, they definitely feel unique and challenging in some ways! (Except Sewvia, She's a MONSTER *-*) The developers are listening to the community and the changes on the autocast was game changer. The graphics are super cute, the game is difficult and Axel is a Daddy... I'm looking forward to see where the game is going and gimme the beach levels and an Endless mode! @_@ Pretty please.

At release, there are too few builds and the gameplay lacks variety overall. Not the "Evolution of Vampire Survivors" as it was deemed by early reviewers and marketing. [*]From the description I expected more crafting, but there's only village repairing for upgrades at the moment. [list] [*]Kiting enemies/mobs is depended on far too much. No strategy. [*]Control on the steamdeck/pad is not very good - as dash "B" button requires you to remove your finger from the directional aiming - so it ends up needing remapped to something you can press while aiming and shooting. [*]Control feels floaty - like you are sliding/hovering around more than walking directionally. [*]The auto-shooting mode is a nice to have, but maybe could be expanded more? Like Bloons aiming options? Target near, target far, target strong, target weak. The auto mode just doesn't feel fully baked here. [*]Each skill on a button is initially overwhelming, but does allow for more intentional gameplay. [*]You can very easily get hit by something you didn't see. The overall zoom level is too close - there isn't enough time for enemies from the top of the map to be seen if you are running straight up. [*]I can't tell what the i-frames are when you dash/dodge. This makes it feel un-reliable. [/list] I'll follow and update review, but for now you aren't missing much in Crafty Survivors.

It is okay. The only reason I do not recommend it, is because of 2 main reasons. The first, this game is extremely repetitive and instead of respecting your time, demands you to grind ridiculous hours doing the same thing with the same few builds they offer. Which brings me to my second point, the builds are fun, but numerically unbalanced. Each new character is more complex than the last, but with nothing to make up for it. Why pick the blacksmith who needs manual control and to sit idle for 5 seconds to build a 2 second weapon, when you can pick the OG chef with auto-attack. Why pick the corn build on the farmer at all? it does the same damage as carrot but also immobilizes you. it reminds me of the Elementalist in Guild Wars 2. 20 extra abilities, but now each ability does 10% the damage.
角色设计很有趣，特别是那个用针线的，但有很多东西要改 中高难度下除非把局外成长拉满，不然前几波一个怪都很难刮死。 同角色也就一两个流派，选好角色就知道这把要玩成什么样没有随机性可言 弹幕不明显，红的蓝的白的弹幕乱飞（尤其是白的），再加上角色的技能特效，死都不知道怎么死的 随机的双倍金币双倍材料关卡强行拖时间，我是完全懒得回头刷一样的关卡的
人物虽然多但是流派就一种，每关的时间太长了，尤其后期要开地图，每个线路都需要打一次图，山脉关一个图加隐藏都有三条路线，一个图要打三遍还不谈失败的情况，因为重复刷图，材料不缺，但是要开地图就要刷图，后期就是为了开地图而刷图，开完图再刷图开地图，非常无聊，总结除了人物技能比较有特色外，就是个关卡设计很失败的类吸血鬼游戏

Despite the promise of way more creative builds, each character realistically only has about 2, due to skills having such heavy synergies that mixing them freely is not really an option. Levels drag on without getting much more interesting, only for the next one to be kind of just the same. Meta-progression is slow and minimal. Five hours in, I have unlocked such bonuses as "+3% attack damage" and "1% faster dodge cooldown". The original promise of this game just doesn't hold up, especially after watching the changes over like a year of patches.

I hate this game. There's something very wrong with it. The camera is about 30% too close to your character, which is often a problem when (in an absolutely bizarre design decision) super-fast worms come charging right for you at random. If they come from top or bottom, you're taking a hit unless you dodge in about 1/4 of a second. Additionally, everything makes visual clutter, and you don't get bonus points for having beefed-up skills that make big, screen-filling effects. Dodging through enemies sometimes hurts you anyways. The skills that pull enemies often pulls them straight through you, damaging you. So many enemies do AOE ground effects which half the time you can't see. When the clutter builds up, it's almost impossible to see the underlying environment which involves trees and such you can't pass through. The character class balance is beyond stupid. It's bizarre. The game is half fantastic: Skills are clever and useful, synergies are good, enemies are a bit samey, progression is almost fine (a little too grindy). But the other half is like it was made by people who've never played games before, or who don't even like them. But hey. Pride day whoopee. Two ladies shack up, even though heretofore if anybody had a preference, it wasn't part of the game. Because it isn't. They're sprites, they don't have lives outside of the pew pew. Yeah this is a good use of priorities.
This game is too difficult and unfun to warrant remaining on my hard drive. EA or not, "EASY" difficulty shouldn't mean "Impossible without a trainer program". Uninstalled. Wish I could get a refund.

The developers seem to think making an excessively grindy game is "fun." I gave the game a fair chance and tried to enjoy it. Even submitted feedback in the discord, their response is generally, "you need more upgrades." Listen, a match shouldn't take me 45+ minutes. Most survivor type games cap it at 30 minutes. It's exhausting and not fun. Sure I could play on "easy" mode for shorter matches, but that's not fun either because you get so little XP that you can hardly level up and try out a kit. I'll update this review if the developers pay more attention to the grind. Maybe they should start a brand new save file and see if they are having fun.

看到很多人都说这游戏难我来说一下吧。真的没有这么难，目前我5角色解锁恶意满满都通了，要想玩得明白一定要了解好角色的机制。 厨师是最中规中矩的，就二个流派烘烤调味流和糖霜蜜饯流，核心是大招上餐，注意一定不要乱拿，比如拿烘烤糖霜啥的，就不好凑出大了。还有就是无论你走哪个流派普工一定要升到3到4级，这样你大招才快，才有续航和伤害，后面成型了10多秒一个大，一个大就回满血基本就稳了。 雕刻家是上限我认为最高的角色，也是我最喜欢的角色，她前期确实难而且坐牢，但有规划度过前期就是最强角色。她的玩法就是前期拿几个木制撑一下，尽快找到自然之拥，等撑到自然之拥3级就有一定续航了。作为一个阵地战角色自然之拥能打打减缓你的压力是她的核心。为啥她上限高就是因为她宝箱那个技能，这个技能吸经验范围大配合她阵地属性成型了经验涨的快是你最早有大师技能等级的角色。配置基本上就是2个木制加上宝箱、自然之拥最后一个守护盾这套，成型了就站着不动就行了。要注意因为是一个阵地角色千万不要到处乱跑，特别是我这种开自动的，因为技能没雕完是不进冷却的。 裁缝我认为是一个下限高但上限也低的角色，她的闪避确实多，但输出基本都要冲进去导致生存没想象那么好，闪避冷却也不算很低后期不怎么跟得上，敌方远程多的时候还会撞弹幕上。续航能力也比较低，回血的噬魂布也是近距离的闪避时候不容易吸到血，稳定吸血要到6级才有。流派比较固定，都是走雷针流派。注意不要去拿那个蓄力暴击那玩意，纯坑，最高难度没命给你蓄。当然敌方攻击频率高的情况她还是最优解，比如森林关的诅咒宝箱。 然后是樵夫，樵夫是一个基本没法自动的角色。又因为蓄力机制导致一根手指必须安装蓄力键键盘玩限制走位所以我用的手柄。这角色很强，基本思路就是旋风斩就行了，旋风斩解锁了全屏就稳了，然后注意不要点滑行，没屁用，双人杂技点一级就行了，后期基本斧斧不会下来的，然后随便点一些斧斧技能就行。要注意点了树木加伤中期压力不打可以不上斧斧让它多去砍点树。 最后是农女，农女和雕刻很像，都是阵地型的，前期可能比雕刻还弱只有挥3下水壶，还好这游戏前面没杀到怪出怪会停，慢慢磨到2级出一个种子就好起来了。尽量不要用胡萝卜，最后一下冲进去不一定回得来。她的回血手段多但效率都不是特别高要注意一点。还有她技能虽然不像雕刻师没雕不刷新但尽量也不要乱跑，毕竟阵地型的。 目前我只解锁了这5个角色，其他的应该也不会难到那里去，写这么多只像说明这游戏真没这么难，你要理解每位角色的特性。当然这游戏比较肝和角色技能的平衡做得确实不咋好。

I want to start with one thing. This game has some awesome potential. That being said, while I was playing, something felt off. I couldn't place my finger on it, so I kept going, enjoying the characters you can play and their unique individual playstyles. I then realized that I was unable to dodge certain attacks, and was taking more damage than I do in other similar games. Upon further investigation, I found that the direction I was pushing would randomly "stick" and I would not be able to stop my character or correct their movement once this started. it happens for about 1 or 2 seconds every couple of minutes, but the amount of damage you take while getting hit makes it an unforgivable bug. To put the frosting on the cake, the developers have come out insisting there "is no problem" or that it must be some processing or lag error from my very high speed internet or $3000 custom built computer that experiences zero issues while playing brand new AAA titles. Until this seemingly simple issue is at least acknowledged as a developer side issue, I cannot recommend this game for any price. I would be willing to change this review to positive if I receive any new information regarding this problem, but it seems like the developers would rather stick their heads in the sand and blame the consumer rather than providing a better gaming experience for their paying customers.

I think I'm going to be playing this one for a while... it feels very satisfying to provoke chain reactions and find synergies between different skills. Love it that the game keeps throwing new characters at you regularly too, so you never really feel you're stalling. Not sure if there's a way to change that in Settings, but I was a bit confused by the way the skills get linked to buttons in the order they are acquired, so I find myself having to relearn the commands every time I start a new stage. All in all, great game though, fun, addictive and to the point.

I really really really wanted to like this game, but unfortunately it's just too much of a chore to play. As far as games like it goes it's quite unique and does a lot of cool things. Each character plays significantly different from each other leading to a very different experience for each one. This however is where the main issue with this game lies. These types of games are typically quite grindy, requiring hundreds of runs to complete. That's fine because they're also usually quite simple in moment to moment gameplay. Most of the thinking happens when choosing your builds, not in actually executing them. That means you can kinda just turn your brain off and chill while playing these games and grinding out the goals. This game is not like that. Each character has so much going on that you can never just "turn your brain off". Every character (out of the 6 I've unlocked so far) requires you to think carefully about everything you're doing, as each character has complex mechanics and interactions that you have to consider when using your abilities. At first this was great, but when you're confronted with the immense grind this game requires (much much more grindy than other similar games) then this kind of complexity quickly becomes exhausting. This issue is compounded by how enemies are, for the most part, pretty boring and simple. All the complexity is just in how your character executes their abilities. It is not matched or built on in any way by the enemies, meaning the strategies you use for hour 1 are the strategies you'll be using the whole time. Ultimately this game needed either less grind (shorter runs, fewer runs required, or some combination of the two) and/or more quickly appearing differences in gameplay. Complex combat is fun, but the exact same complex combat with 0 changes for hours is just a chore.

玩了许久，最后还是改了差评。虽然总体还可以吧，角色很多，局外养成还可以强化技能机制，算是内容比较丰富的一款幸存者了，不过真的太肝了，关卡搞那么多干嘛呢？还带隐藏支线，最后也就可能多拿个宝箱，奖励还不多，我还不如刷一把高难度金币双倍的图，随便几百万到手，这种设计完全是为了肝而肝。而且后期的副本有严重难度曲线的问题，1级出门碰的怪直接就一千血量，而有的角色一级普攻才30左右的伤害，大招一级还用不了（珠宝师），请问这种角色怎么玩？爽点在哪？好歹开局出一点白给的怪送点经验吧？很多角色想通关真的难度太高了，后期副本血多，怪密，有远程，有追踪，有高速屏幕外突然蹦出来的，有大范围AOE，机制太多了，怪又难杀，难度过于高了。 这游戏大剑流铁匠应该是唯一真神，开局强能清杂兵升级，对局中后期有高格挡和超大AOE，击杀还能回血，而且只要点几个技能升满，之后升级可以一直拿金币，资源更多，成型后除了BOSS关都是直接挂机解放双手。武器选大剑，然后技能点50耐久一次AOE伤害的技能（自动）、普攻、特殊技能（自动）、加暴击率的被动、火炉（自动）、磨炼武器（自动），以上只要50耐久的技能点到4级就基本可以开自动挂机了，但是不要开局就强行去升级，这玩意开局不好用，原地罚站很容易掉血。 还有个女农民西蓝花锤子加南瓜也挺强，全屏AOE且带眩晕，不过高难的话开局打不动杂兵，升级太难，只能低难度无双，而且不能挂机。

As someone who has played this game from very early access, I just CANNOT recommend it to new players, not in its current state. This review is from the perspective of playing exclusively on the hardest difficulty (which some people claim is meant to be poorly designed), having played every single character multiple times, and nearly having 100% achievement completion. Issue #1: Starting with the biggest issue first: BUGS. Just mountains and mountains of bugs that have existed since early stages of development that for whatever reason the creators still refuse to fix. I was willing to overlook most of these during early access figuring the devs would eventually fix it, but these bugs are completely inexcusable in the final release of the game. Bosses spawning outside of the map, forcing you to restart a 40-50 minute play through. Creatures infinitely spawning experience locking you into a level up screen until the game eventually crashes from too many items spawning. Assets not despawning properly resulting in massive lag. Massive lag caused by poor optimization and bad design decisions, biggest culprits being Mausolea or jewlia who will both result in your game running at 1 FPS until their abilities end. Being hit by invisible attacks or attacks that just didn't load in properly. Charging enemies are supposed to have an indicator of what direction they are going, except when they randomly change their charge distance, some will charge clear off screen, others will move 2 feet and immediately change direction to hit you, some will charge in a completely different direction from the indicator. Issue #2: game balance. It's bad. I'm not talking about how some characters are harder than others, I mean that some characters are not just harder to play, but so incredibly weak as to be a chore to play (lumberjack, builder, alchemist), these characters have poorly designed kits, low damage, and extremely limited playstyle. This has been an issue the players have raised for a very long time, and the devs had multiple opportunities to fix it with various changes they made to the game, instead they just left those characters to rot. This leads into the next issue Issue 3: A survivor game that tried to be a bullet hell (and failed). From the early levels and characters the game was obviously going for the typical survivor like playstyle, fight waves of enemies that run at you until you become strong enough to demolish everything and eventually fight a boss. Later stages this design choice completely changed to being a bullet hell where enemies will launch dozens of projectiles at you, enemies will charge at you from off screen, enemies will lurk just off screen to get a cheap shot on you when you move too close, some enemies will straight up attack you from across the entire map forcing you to run around trying to figure out where they are. This problem is made all the worse by the character kits. Many characters are designed with a survivor gameplay in mind (standing still or staying in a limited area using turret style skills, extremely limited dodging ability, and skills that slow you down), but being forced to run around the map means these characters are just too annoying to play. Issue 4: lack of planning by the developers. One of the main features of Crafty Survivors is the town building aspect, where upgrading buildings will provide you with buffs. Some buildings will even provide new and interesting ways to change your playstyle. Sounds great right? The issue? They don't work with character kits. I'll use Stoverick the chef as an example, as he is one of the first characters you will play as. One of the buildings provides potions that give new abilities to select when a character levels up. But they don't interact with the character kits at all. One potion lets you throw beehives, stoverick gains stacks for his ultimate attack when he kills enemies that have been marked by his other skills, but the potion abilities don't apply these marks, meaning no stacks for his strongest attack, so there is ZERO reason to ever pick these abilities. This gets even worse with characters like the alchemist and jeweler that have to combo their skills, so choosing these extra abilities end up being a complete waste because it breaks the entire kit and uses up valuable weapon slots, or forces you to use up your limited banish ability to remove these worthless abilities from the selection pool. Next we have the skill trees, each character can get 20 points to allocate to their skill tree to change their playstyle slightly, Some characters like the farmer get a whole complicated tree to customize your playstyle with her, others like the builder get a very linear path that forces you to play them in one specific way. Others like Sewvia get a skill tree that doesn't interact with her kit in any meaningful way and merely changes her basic attacks. Remember those potions that give you new abilities I mentioned earlier? Yeah this is another reason they're complete garbage. Issue #5: personal views of the game. This section is largely my own personal issues with game design choices, some people will likely disagree. skill opacity is useless when player abilities are layered over enemies. Even playing with 30 opacity on my skills I frequently cannot see attacks or enemies underneath the dozens of effects my character is throwing around, and god forbid I use an ability that creates a gas cloud because the enemy gas clouds are THE EXACT SOME COLOR making them invisible. Aggressive field materials shouldn't be minibosses! These enemies have the most obnoxious abilities combined with 4-5x the health of a standard enemy. Undodgeable attacks shouldn't exist in this type of game, this goes back to the bullet hell change, but multiple later stage bosses were given large screen covering abilities that cannot be blocked or dodged, you just have to try and get to the safe zone and hope your dash doesn't launch you too far. All of this is why even with hundreds of hours into this game, I just cannot recommend what it has become. What started as a unique and very enjoyable survivor-like has become an unrecognizable wannabe bullet-hell riddled with bugs, questionable design choices, and poor game balance.

On the surface the game is an interesting take on horde survivors. The different characters have unique playstyles and it can be quite a bit of fun. However the game doesn't seem to be that well thought out, in some cases it seems like stuff was thrown in because it sounds good, but not very well tested how they work when actually played out. An example would be one skill that forces your character to stand still for 2 seconds only to gain a buff that guarantees the next hit to be critical. In a game like this, unless you have a suitable build, standing still is a death sentence and the character with that skill is one designed from the ground up to be mobile and that is beside the point of the pathetic payout you get for that. Another issue to me is that skills are not autocast by default and some skills are definitely meant to be used manually, this is in my opinion counterproductive in a game like this. You have to keep track of your own character and a ton of enemies and their attacks, having to keep track of your skills at the same time is rather taxing. There is a reason why in other horde survivors skills are usually autocast and even aiming is often done automatically. It's one reason why I tried to play the lumberjack only once. Charging his skills, keeping track of the enemies and the stupid companion that might very well be on the other side of the map, it was for me unplayable. Also the charging of his main attack seemed bugged, I often had to push the button twice before he started to charge up. Also the charge was lost when I leveled up. The game is also stingy with information. Unlike other games like this, where level up for skills usually only affect stuff like cooldown, damage, range, etc, the skills here sometimes get additional effects. It would be nice to be able to look up the skills and the evolutions somewhere. Also what is really counterintuitive is that some of the resource items double as healing. If it's mentioned somewhere I didn't notice it and since enemies drop hearts as healing, I did not expect acorns or mushrooms being also healing items was rather counterintuitive. The help menu seems to only be available in the character select screen, which is honestly stupid, because it barely has any information that would be relevant to only the character selection. Balance is a bit of a mess, to the point where at least to me it seems almost like the higher difficulties are actually easier than the lower ones. With the increased number of enemies you get more level ups, once you get a build going the increased health of the enemies doesn't matter too much anymore. The damage of the enemies is the same, regardless of the difficulty and due to an increase in material gain you actually have more healing on higher difficulties. You might be a bit more likely to get hit, but you actually have it easier to recover from the hits you do get. You get passive stat boosts by building the town, the resources for that come from the various stages, so far I didn't really had a problem with a lack of resources, but it might get grindy eventually. Overall the game can be fun, but I think the developers really need to put in some more work before I would consider recommending it to anyone.

When I first started this game, it captured my attention, stole me from another game I purchased in a pack. I am a fanatic for the bullet-heaven genre, I play them all as I am able, steam, ps5, switch, anything I can reach. Crafty Survivors surprised me with some fresh ideas....Initially. Clocking a bit over 25 hours at the point of this review, it's safe to say that yes, you will get your value's worth of game play. However, this is a genre of game centered around the time sink, repeating runs to get a bit further, to grow stronger, to become an unstoppable demon on the field, only to find another level of being you must grind more to overcome. It's a study, a development both personal and casual, understanding mechanics, exploiting builds, all that dopamine crashing stuff. Crafty Survivors fails at this point. The levels are repetitive and pointless, leaving little to the imagination in terms of build and strategy. Some levels have multiple paths, which if main, you must finish the zone at least twice; others, there is an 'explorer' mode, meaning you can just run it again as a character that can unlock the next path with no opposition, a blank map to tediously rush through on the borders just to use a singular skill for an exit. There are quite a few characters to choose from, except they take so long to unlock, they may as well not exist at all, save for those 'explorer' mode unlockable paths. With Crafty Survivors, you gain a character named Sewvia fairly early on; there is no point in any capacity to use anyone but her. Dodge is so incredibly important in this game, and everyone I have seen thus far has ONE dodge....Sewvia starts with three, which also damages and ties in to other necessary skills that stun and decimate, and can get up to six dodges that have a good chance of not depleting, increasing her power with each. You do get the building options in your town to increase power, mats, all that good stuff....but it costs so much gold, so many new mats, that it's only ever efficient to progress as fast as possible. What's more, gold is the only true currency to ever care about; there are zone spawn that drop unique mats, but once you collect one, you can purchase it with a merchant that appears so frequently even at base level, why should you grind at all? You can use a bank that accrues interest per run, and you can get merchants that sell mats you have encountered as mentioned, some requiring different matter of payment. So obviously, prioritize the banking, and the game becomes incredibly trivial....Except for the fact that difficulty spikes to absurd and unexpected levels, upgrade cost becoming grossly unbalanced. You even receive buildings that automatically accrue pricey mats, so why do little else then dump your gold into them? There comes a moment where you unlock statues that can increase, decrease, or eliminate enemy spawn time; with Sewvia, the only option is to max enemy spawn just so you can complete the boring levels quicker for power; NO OTHER CHARACTER CAN SURVIVE THIS AS I HAVE SEEN REASONABLY THUS FAR. There is not a single reason to not use this spawn statue other than wanting to win as someone other than Sewvia, though this drags out the game play to unbearable levels of monotony. When you encounter bosses, known mostly as Corrupted Heroes, the unbalance begins to reel at your mind. No matter your health, no matter your strength, these bosses are so insanely balanced towards dodging, that your choice in Sewvia truly becomes apparent. I do enjoy this game, I will continue to grind until I've locked it all down...But it's a chore, a thing I do while the game is muted and my music is blaring. I did see some comments about rush, lack of proper funding, and that is truly disheartening. There is so much here to love, so much to look to for the genre's progression, and I wish only the best to the devs to build on this grand base of a game. However, there are existing titles that do it better, give you more for your time and life. Last comes builds. I do love that each character has their own pool, but....Honestly there is truly only one 'right' way to play each character. You do unlock the standard 'banish' 'reserve' and 'reroll', but there is barely a point to this, especially for how long it takes to unlock, and how you have no idea when these upgrades become available (buildings don't tell you what they unlock before upgrades, one at a time with increasing cost, only ever seeing what's next after you pay for the first). The pool of skills is so shallow, that you get what you want too easily. Further, there is no point at all in banishing 'skills' since you have five slots, and once they are filled, nothing else will show, save for an even smaller pool of passives, which you only need three points in. Passives are so limited as well as congruent per character, that banish two or three, and you have a clear choice every level. I write this as a negative review purely for the love of the genre, and those seeking more like me. It's worth it, honestly, play it if you can, have the stomach, the need as I do. I'm likely to sink another 25 hours myself....But I'm diehard, stubborn; there is too little here to recommend when there are more fleshed out options. I truly hope the devs become notable enough, supported, that their visions can be met. Because, in the end, why I am stuck playing this shell of a game, is it 'has' that spice, that idea, that scratch to the itch, that 'nothing a sequel can't fix' feeling that burns at your thoughts, that you wish for, wait for, yearn for.

Fun at first, grindy in the middle, fun at the end again. From the "Survivors" name you might expect something like Vampire Survivors: get abilities until the screen is full of bullets and the enemies are dying en masse. After you see the dodge mechanics and bosses you might expect something more like Death Must Die. Instead, it seems more like it's intended to be a more skill-based action roguelike (something like Death Must Die is slowly moving towards). Good character selection eventually, but most characters unlocked early are hard to use and it takes until almost the very end to unlock some of the most fun ones (Keyra / Newsom). The game works against itself by having some characters drop special resources (Rodrigo for fish, Mausolea for candy) that you need to progress, and requiring them in sufficient amounts that you practically have to run these characters for most of the game. On the positive side, Rodrigo is incredibly strong (high damage with crab trap, easy to get lots of hearts with the net and the basic attack) and Mausolea is my favourite character (I run a summonless build with an Elixired Fungal Vortex). You can get fish from the Fisherman's Hut and candy from the Graveyard, but you need to play the characters in the relevant zones first before you can unlock the levels for the areas required (for the Hut, the Graveyard does not have this issue outside the Haunted Grounds). I played most of the game on Malignous with Cursed Bait (which I only turned off for some of the end-game character-specific boss fights). The levels are long enough with the Bait that I dread to think what it must have been like going through before it. I swapped down to Normal to halve the number of enemies (and their health) after the first three zones, which made progress slightly faster. Even with all the difficulty modifiers I never had much of a problem passing the levels with Rodrigo, or some of the other characters after I unlocked their Forge and Tailor upgrades. The first Tailor upgrade to double the invincibility time on dodge is a game-changer that means you can do things like dodge into a crowd of enemies, fire a shot, then escape out the other side to churn through them faster. The Forge and Tailor upgrades also work against playing multiple characters, as you invest points into each character individually. Some are easier to upgrade than others: Rodrigo needs his fish, Mausolea needs her candy, the other characters need resources you can buy in the shop. After you unlock the Farm, you can grow vegetables and sell them to have as much gold as you'll need. The Bank is a terrible way to make gold comparatively. Most upgrades are very weak and progress feels very slow. Food-wise, the foods that give attack and skill damage over time, and Stone Soup that gives block chance over time seem stand-outs. Block chance is really good and it's difficult to get much of it, and anything that makes you better over time ends up giving a pretty decent boost. For statues, the only stand-out is the one that lets normal enemies drop chests, which gives you loads of levels. I was glad for the Laboratory offering non-character-specific skills, some of which seemed better than most character-specific skills. Fungal Vortex especially can one-shot a boss: I'm not sure specifically how, but I think if you can pull enough clouds, especially black clouds, the tornados can end up doing 40k damage each (and it charges all the way on auto unless you dodge, which is appreciated). The crab claw does a lot of damage but is hard to aim. The mud circle, sand circle and Hoggert roar were all appreciated as decently damaging character-centred AoE attacks, and all the Spectral weapons are quite damaging (and the sword offers sustain) but tricky to aim. You can also pull in an Elixir just for the passive and banish the attacks, as you have a lot of free banishes. Specific complaints I have: rerolls, banishes and reserves appear to have no key assigned, so you have to use the mouse for these, which is a bit awkward. The late-game Dungeons and Overgrown Lizards challenge sends the adventurers in the order mage, cleric, archer, thief, warrior. The warrior is the easiest by far, and the mage is the hardest and most annoying to fight, so I would have rather these were swapped to give you a chance to level up against an easier opponent. The mage teleports often, making it hard to do damage, has a large undodgable grid attack, and has an ice attack which 1) hits you with an ice block, which 2) fires off tornados after it hits and 3) has a damaging circle around it. With dodge invincibility boosted you can dodge the initial attack and just run out the circle before the invincibility fades; without the boost I don't know how you're supposed to deal with this. As it's a late-game challenge maybe it's just balanced around you having it. With Cursed Bait, the caverns summon masses of enemies right at the start, and on some levels this makes them lag tremendously -- e.g. the bears. It also makes the levels much harder, but this is also fun.
